Life of a Fabric Data Agent Request A top-down flow diagram. A user question enters the agent, which selects a relevant data source using the source's description, schema, and example queries. The agent then fetches that source's schema under the requesting user's own credentials, assembles a prompt for a managed Azure OpenAI Assistant, and generates a read-only query in the source's native language (SQL, DAX, or KQL). The query executes under the user's identity so results never exceed what that user could already see, and Purview DLP policies apply on top. A successful path returns an answer capped at 25 rows and 25 columns; three failure branches short-circuit the flow: cross-region capacity mismatch, unsupported unstructured content, and a DLP block.
Fabric Data Agent — request orchestration internals What happens between a question landing and an answer returning, including the governance and identity checks along the way
pipeline step
governance gate
blocked / fails
1 Question arrives
User natural-language question — A question submitted to a published data agent from chat, Copilot, Foundry, or a custom app.
Natural-language prompt from Fabric chat, Copilot, an Azure AI Foundry orchestrator, or a multi-agent app — carries the caller's identity with it
2
Source selection — The agent picks which attached source (of up to five) is relevant, using description, schema, and example queries together.
Source selection
Prompt assembly (managed Azure OpenAI) — Question, fetched schema, and creator instructions/example queries are assembled into a prompt for a Microsoft-managed Azure OpenAI Assistant.
Agent picks the most relevant of its up-to-5 attached sources (lakehouse, warehouse, semantic model, KQL DB, Graph) based on developer instructions and example queries
3 Governance precedence check Org policy → workspace/role settings → developer instructions → this end-user prompt, evaluated in that order; higher layers can narrow or override what happens next
Failure: region mismatch — The agent cannot execute when its workspace capacity and the source's capacity are in different regions.
Purview DLP / access-restriction policies are evaluated here too — they can block the query outright even if the agent is otherwise permitted to read the source
may block or strip results
4 Schema + instructions grounding <g data-node-id="schema-fetch" role="group"s identity)" tabindex="0" aria-label="Schema fetch (caller's identity)"> Schema fetch (caller's identity) — The agent fetches the target source's schema using the requesting user's own credentials.
Agent reads the selected source's schema and the developer's instructions/example queries to ground how it will phrase the generated query
5 Query generation — read-only
Read-only query generation (NL2SQL/DAX/KQL) — The agent generates a read-only query in the source's native language, never a write statement.
Source-specific generator emits SQL (lakehouse/warehouse), DAX (semantic model), KQL (Eventhouse), or a Graph query — never create/update/delete
6 <g data-node-id="query-execution" role="group"s identity" tabindex="0" aria-label="Execution under caller's identity"> Execution under caller's identity — The generated query runs against the source under the requesting user's own permissions.
Execution — under the caller's own identity
Executes with the requesting user's credentials and permissions, so results never exceed what that user could already see; RLS/CLS on semantic models still applies Read on a Power BI semantic model is enough — Build is not required. Eventhouse KQL databases are queried in place, with no data movement
7 Answer returned with query transparency
Answer returned (capped, query-transparent) — A capped result — max 25 rows and 25 columns — is returned with the generated query visible for transparency.
Result set plus the generated SQL/DAX/KQL is surfaced back to the caller, capped at 25 rows × 25 columns per response — including follow-up turns in the same session
BRANCHES THAT STOP OR SHRINK THE ANSWER (grounded in known antipatterns)
Region mismatch → query fails If the agent's workspace capacity and the data source's workspace capacity sit in different regions, execution cannot proceed — a lakehouse and agent capacity must be co-located to succeed at step 6.
Unsupported content → no query generated
Failure: unsupported unstructured content — The agent cannot directly query PDF, DOCX, TXT, or standalone lakehouse files unless exposed as tables.
Standalone unstructured files (PDF, DOCX,
TXT) and lakehouse files that were never ingested/exposed as tables are outside the agent's reach — step 2 cannot select a generator for content it can't see as a table.
Purview DLP → blocked or redacted
Failure: Purview DLP block — A Purview DLP or access-restriction policy blocks the query or strips sensitive results even when the agent had read permission.
Even when the agent is technically permitted
Purview governance gate — Instruction precedence and Purview DLP/access-restriction policy apply before query generation.
to read a source, a DLP or access-restriction
policy evaluated at step 3 can stop the query from running, or strip sensitive values out of the answer before it reaches the caller.
